info.title: pqc-config — CLI for PostQuantum.Configuration
info.description: Command-line companion to PostQuantum.Configuration. Seal (protect), open (unprotect), and rotate keys for encrypted configuration values from a shell or CI pipeline, backed by a persisted PostQuantum.KeyManagement keyring. Bulk-seal or re-seal whole appsettings.json files atomically (protect-file / reprotect-file), inspect a token's non-secret metadata without any keys (inspect), and — on .NET 10+ — generate hybrid ML-KEM-768 + ECDH P-256 recipient key pairs (keygen), seal to a recipient's public key (--recipient), and migrate a keyring-sealed file onto post-quantum hybrid wrapping (reprotect-file --to-recipient). Read values from stdin to keep secrets out of shell history. See the PostQuantum.Configuration package for the library.

x-inspectra.cliParsedTitle: pqc-config — encrypt configuration values with PostQuantum.Configuration

commands.name: audit
commands.description:
Keyless scan of a JSON config file for plaintext values that look like
secrets (heuristic). Exit 1 if any are found — CI/pre-commit friendly.

commands.name: check
commands.description:
Verify every pqc.v1 token in a JSON file decrypts with the given key
source; --require asserts keys that MUST be protected. Exit 1 on any
failure — a pre-deploy gate. Plaintext is never printed.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Show a token's non-secret metadata (key id, provider) — no keys needed.

commands.name: keygen
commands.description: Generate a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + ECDH P-256 recipient key pair (.NET 10+).

commands.name: protect
commands.description: Seal a value into a pqc.v1 token (creates the keyring on first use).

commands.name: protect-file
commands.description: Seal selected string values in a JSON config file, in place (atomic).

commands.name: reprotect-file
commands.description:
Re-seal every pqc.v1 token in a JSON config file — onto the active key
after a rotate, or onto a hybrid recipient with --to-recipient.

commands.name: rotate
commands.description: Add a fresh active key (same passphrase, new salt); old tokens still open.

commands.name: unprotect
commands.description: Recover the plaintext from a token.

options.name: --keyring
options.description: Path to the keyring file (required unless --recipient / inspect / --dry-run).

options.name: --recipient
options.description:
Hybrid key file instead of a keyring (.NET 10+): the public key
seals; decrypting needs the private key file.

options.name: --to-recipient
options.description:
reprotect-file: re-seal onto this recipient's PUBLIC key —
migrates a keyring-sealed file onto post-quantum hybrid wrapping.

options.name: --public
options.description: keygen: where to write the public key file (never overwrites).

options.name: --private
options.description: keygen: where to write the PRIVATE key file (never overwrites).

options.name: --require
options.description: check: keys that must exist AND be protected tokens.

options.name: --passphrase
options.description: KEK passphrase. Prefer the PQC_PASSPHRASE env var instead.

options.name: --value
options.description:
Value to protect. If omitted, read from stdin.
value on stdin avoids the issue entirely and keeps it out of your shell history.

options.name: --token
options.description: Token to unprotect/inspect. If omitted, read from stdin.

options.name: --context
options.description: Optional context bound into the token (swap resistance).

options.name: --file
options.description:
JSON file for protect-file / reprotect-file (strict JSON: a
rewrite would destroy comments, so files with comments are rejected).

options.name: --keys
options.description:
protect-file: exact keys to seal ('Section:Sub:Name' paths).
A key that is missing or not a string value is an error.

options.name: --section
options.description: protect-file: seal every string value under this section.

options.name: --all
options.description: protect-file: seal every string value in the file.

options.name: --bind-key
options.description:
Bind each value's configuration key as its context
(pairs with AddEncrypted(..., bindKeyAsContext: true)).

options.name: --dry-run
options.description:
protect-file / reprotect-file: print the keys that would change
(one per line, stdout) and leave the file untouched.
Use --option=value (with '=') for any value that starts with '-', e.g.
